narrativeReportMd:
# OperationOutcome R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No local R4-valid `OperationOutcome` instance pattern was found that becomes invalid solely because of the `OperationOutcome` StructureDefinition in R6. The material local risk is the opposite direction: R6 widens required terminology for `issue.severity` and `issue.code`, so R6 OperationOutcome instances using new codes are not cleanly valid as R4 and can break strict R4 enum/codegen clients.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 and R6 `StructureDefinition/OperationOutcome` snapshots and differentials, package indexes, package metadata, and the local ValueSet/CodeSystem resources for the three OperationOutcome-specific bindings. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and `Extension` changes were excluded from findings and listed out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The element tree is stable: no local elements were added, removed, renamed, moved, or re-cardinalized, and no local datatype/reference changes were found. Migration attention should focus on terminology: `IssueSeverity` adds `success`; `IssueType` adds `success` and `limited-filter`; `issue.details` points to a renamed/example ValueSet that still composes from the operation-outcome code system.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `OperationOutcome:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:OperationOutcome.issue.severity:53c7e5` and `OperationOutcome:TERMINOLOGY_BINDING:OperationOutcome.issue.code:684920`. Both are required bindings widened in R6, creating R6→R4 representability and strict-client runtime risks rather than R4→R6 validation breaks.

## Findings requiring human review
Only the `issue.details` example-binding canonical change requires review if an implementation treats example binding URLs as generated enum or configuration identities. Its validation impact is low because example bindings do not constrain base instances.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The new required codes appear justified as more precise outcome reporting. Less disruptive alternatives existed, such as retaining older codes with more specific `details` codings, but those alternatives would lose base-level computable semantics.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the base `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and `Extension` reports for inherited changes that affect all resources, especially `language`, contained-resource constraints, and extension invariants.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `OperationOutcome` keeps the same resource identity and element structure from R4 to R6. The main migration concerns are new required-binding codes for `issue.severity` and `issue.code`, plus a low-risk example-binding canonical change on `issue.details`. Confidence is high for computable deltas, with some uncertainty about official rationale and external terminology publication details.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Generated models and validators should tolerate or map the new R6 codes when exchanging with R4 systems. R4→R6 structural migration is straightforward for local `OperationOutcome` fields, but R6→R4 conversion needs policies for `severity=success`, `code=success`, and `code=limited-filter`. Systems that key behavior off the `issue.details` example ValueSet URL should update configuration to the R6 canonical.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high because both assigned StructureDefinitions were present, their local element IDs match exactly, and the relevant required ValueSets are simple local includes of complete local CodeSystems. Confidence would improve with official diffs, rendered narrative pages, and a terminology.hl7.org publication comparison for the external `operation-outcome` code system used by the example binding.

findings.title: OperationOutcome.issue.severity required binding adds success

oldState.summary: Required binding to IssueSeverity 4.0.1 with fatal, error, warning, and information.

binding.description: How the issue affects the success of the action.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 ValueSet composes all codes from local complete CodeSystem `http://hl7.org/fhir/issue-severity`; the local code system contains `fatal`, `error`, `warning`, and `information`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required `issue.severity` to be one of four severity codes.

newState.summary: Required binding to IssueSeverity 6.0.0-ballot4 with a new success code.

binding.description: How the issue affects the success of the action.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 local CodeSystem adds `success` with definition "The operation completed successfully." No R4 severity codes were removed or redefined in the local code system comparison.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the element mandatory but allows a successful outcome to be expressed using `severity=success`.

facts.note: Required binding means this is valid R6 base content but not valid against the R4 required value set.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element has the same id, path, type, cardinality, and binding name in both versions; only the versioned required ValueSet content changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4→R6 validation break because all R4 severity codes remain valid in the R6 local code system. It is a direct R6→R4 problem: an R6 instance with `severity=success` fails the R4 required binding. Strict R4 generated enums, switch statements, or validators may reject or mishandle the new code.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassifying or rejecting a successful OperationOutcome can affect workflow status handling, although it is unlikely to directly alter clinical facts.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow OperationOutcome to explicitly report successful processing rather than only errors, warnings, or informational notes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6-preserving alternative is needed because the R6 binding only adds `success`; all R4 severity codes remain valid.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal--explicitly distinguishing successful OperationOutcome responses--is reasonable. The local terminology adds `success` without removing any R4 severity code, and the existing finding classifies the impact as `hardInstanceBreaking: No` and `affectedDirection: R6-to-R4`. Under the calibration rules, this is not an R4-to-R6 base-design break; the remaining cost is closed-enum and down-conversion risk for R4 consumers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping R6 severity limited to `information` and expressing success in `issue.code`, `details`, or text would preserve closed R4 enum compatibility for downstream R4 exchange, but it is not an alternative needed to preserve R4-valid instances in R6. It is mainly an R6-to-R4 mapping or semantic tradeoff, and it would make success less directly computable in the base required severity field.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Using `information` plus details can support R6-to-R4 mapping, but that is migration guidance rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R4 binds severity to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/issue-severity|4.0.1` with strength required.
R6 binds severity to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/issue-severity|6.0.0-ballot4` with strength required.

details.text: R6 severity=success mapped to R4 information for backward exchange.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example isolates the severity change by using an R4-valid `issue.code`. The migration example is lossy because R4 has no exact severity equivalent for `success`.

findings.narrativeMd: `OperationOutcome.issue.severity` is still required and structurally unchanged, but its required value set now includes `success`. This widens R6 and helps express successful processing, but R4 systems that modeled the field as a closed enum of four values will not recognize the fifth value.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using `fatal`, `error`, `warning`, or `information` remain valid against the R6 required binding. R6 instances using `success` are not valid R4 instances without transformation. Runtime failures are most likely in strict deserializers, generated enum parsers, exhaustive UI severity mappings, and validation gateways.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, no transform is needed for existing severity values. For R6→R4, decide whether to map `success` to `information`, drop the issue, or preserve the original R6 code in `details`, an extension, or out-of-band metadata. Add tests for strict enum parsing and round-trip conversion of successful OperationOutcome responses.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding a required-binding code is backward-compatible for R4→R6 validation but not for R6→R4 consumers. The likely goal could have been achieved with `information` plus detail text/coding, but that would make success less standardized and less discoverable. The chosen design is reasonable if R6 prioritizes explicit success semantics over closed-enum compatibility with R4.

findings.title: OperationOutcome.issue.code required binding adds success and limited-filter

oldState.summary: Required binding to IssueType 4.0.1 without success or limited-filter.

binding.description: A code that describes the type of issue.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 ValueSet composes all codes from complete local CodeSystem `http://hl7.org/fhir/issue-type`.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required `issue.code` to be one of the R4 IssueType codes; neither `success` nor `limited-filter` was available.

newState.summary: Required binding to IssueType 6.0.0-ballot4 with success and limited-filter added.

binding.description: A code that describes the type of issue.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 local CodeSystem adds `limited-filter` and `success`. No R4 IssueType codes were removed or had display/definition/parent changes in the local comparison.

semanticText.comment: Code values should align with the severity, but there are no strict rules about which severities must be used with which codes.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 widens the required issue type vocabulary and adds non-normative guidance that code values should generally align with severity.

facts.note: Represents partial application of search filters.

facts.newValue: Code values should align with the severity, but no strict rules are imposed.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element has the same id, path, type, cardinality, binding name, and required strength in both versions; the bound code system content is widened.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The required IssueType binding is widened, not narrowed. Existing R4 IssueType codes remain valid in R6, so this is not an old-valid/new-invalid break. However, R6 instances using `success` or `limited-filter` are invalid against the R4 required binding and can break strict R4 enum handling.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `limited-filter` can carry operationally important search-result caveats; dropping or mis-mapping it may cause consumers to over-trust returned data.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent successful OperationOutcome responses and warn when search filtering was only partially applied.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6-preserving alternative is needed because R6 widens the required IssueType value set while retaining the R4 codes.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goals--representing successful outcomes and partially applied search filters--are reasonable terminology additions. The local R6 IssueType code system adds `success` and nested `limited-filter` while retaining the R4 codes, so existing R4-valid `issue.code` values remain valid in R6. The compatibility problem is R6-to-R4 representability and strict R4 enum handling, not old-valid/new-invalid base validation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have avoided new IssueType codes and asked producers to use existing broad codes such as `informational`, `processing`, or `business-rule` plus `details` coding/text. That would be a down-conversion-friendly modeling choice, but it is not required to preserve R4 instances in R6 and would make the new conditions less visible to generic clients.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Mapping `success` or `limited-filter` to broader R4 codes can ease R6-to-R4 exchange, but it is a lossy conversion policy rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R4 binds issue code to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/issue-type|4.0.1` with strength required.
R6 binds issue code to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/issue-type|6.0.0-ballot4` with strength required.

evidence.quote: Some search filters might not have applied on all results.

evidence.detail: R6 adds guidance that issue codes should align with severity but does not impose a strict invariant.

issue.diagnostics: Some requested filters were not applied to every returned result.

details.text: R6 issue.code=limited-filter mapped to a broader R4 issue type with original code retained in details.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example isolates the IssueType addition by using an R4-valid severity. The migration example is illustrative and lossy because R4 has no exact `limited-filter` IssueType code.

findings.narrativeMd: `OperationOutcome.issue.code` remains mandatory and bound with required strength, but R6 adds `success` and `limited-filter` to the IssueType code system. This is a classic cross-version enum hazard: R6 producers can emit valid codes that R4 consumers were not generated to parse.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: All compared R4 IssueType codes are still present in R6, so an R4 instance does not become invalid merely because of this binding. R6 instances using either new code fail R4 required-binding validation unless transformed. Even permissive JSON parsers may have runtime issues if application logic uses exhaustive switches over known R4 issue codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update validators, enum types, UI labels, and business-rule dispatch for `success` and `limited-filter`. For R6→R4 exchange, define explicit maps such as `success`→`informational` or `limited-filter`→`processing`/`business-rule`, and preserve the original R6 code in `details`, an extension, or audit metadata where losslessness matters. Test search responses that include partial-filter warnings.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The additive codes appear useful and avoid overloading broad R4 categories. A backward-compatible alternative would have relied on `details` or profile-specific codes, but that would require out-of-band agreements and make the condition harder for generic clients to detect.

findings.title: OperationOutcome.issue.details example binding points to a different ValueSet canonical

binding.description: A code that provides details as the exact issue.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 ValueSet compose includes `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/operation-outcome`; the local R4 package also contains a matching CodeSystem file.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 used `ValueSet/operation-outcome` as an example value set for detailed error codes.

binding.description: A code that provides details as the exact issue.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R6 ValueSet compose also includes `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/operation-outcome`, but the R6 core package did not include the external CodeSystem resource for a code-by-code comparison.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 changes the example ValueSet canonical while keeping the element optional and the binding strength at example.

facts.note: Both local ValueSets include the same external code system.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element identity, path, cardinality, type, binding name, and binding strength are unchanged; the only local computable change is the example ValueSet canonical URL.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Example bindings do not make base instances invalid when codes fall outside the example set, so this is not a hard validation break. The risk is limited to tooling that treats example binding URLs as generated enum identities, documentation links, or configuration keys.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A stale example binding URL could degrade error-code display or mapping, but should not change the core success/failure meaning of an OperationOutcome.

justification.inferredGoal: Reuse or rename a shared outcome-detail example value set across artifacts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 base-design alternative is needed because the element remains optional and example-bound; base instances are not invalidated by the canonical change.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal appears to be canonical cleanup or reuse of a shared outcome-detail example value set. Because `issue.details` remains `0..1`, keeps type `CodeableConcept`, and keeps binding strength `example`, neither R4 nor R6 base validation should reject instances solely because of this ValueSet URL change. The impact is limited to terminology metadata, generated artifacts, or tools that over-enforce example bindings.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping `ValueSet/operation-outcome` for OperationOutcome or publishing it as a deprecated alias would be friendlier to tools keyed to the old canonical. That is a reasonable metadata-continuity option, but under the calibration rules it is not a backward-compatible base R6 design alternative for a breaking R4-to-R6 issue, because no R4-valid instance pattern needs preservation here.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining the old ValueSet canonical as an alias would reduce tooling churn, but it preserves metadata references rather than R4-valid instance compatibility.

evidence.detail: R6 example ValueSet includes the same external code system.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is needed because an example binding change does not by itself make a base instance valid or invalid. The practical example is a code generator or validation UI needing to update the canonical ValueSet URL it displays for `issue.details`.

findings.narrativeMd: `OperationOutcome.issue.details` keeps the same optional `CodeableConcept` type and example binding strength, but the example ValueSet canonical changes. This is useful migration information for terminology configuration, but it is not a base validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Because the binding strength is `example`, neither R4 nor R6 base validation should reject an instance solely for using a coding outside the named example ValueSet. R6-to-R4 representability risk is therefore low and limited to systems that over-enforce example bindings or key generated artifacts by the ValueSet URL.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update documentation links and generated terminology metadata from `ValueSet/operation-outcome` to `ValueSet/audit-event-outcome-detail-example` for R6. If supporting both versions, treat the two example ValueSets as closely related because both compose from `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/operation-outcome`, but verify external terminology content if exact code lists matter.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably avoidable by retaining the old canonical as an alias, but the low binding strength means the practical compatibility cost is small. The main tradeoff is canonical tidiness versus old tooling references.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is useful only for implementations that generate enums or decision tables from example bindings, or that depend on the R4 package-local `CodeSystem-operation-outcome.json` content.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, baseDefinition, abstract flag, active status, normative standards-status, and FMM 5 status are stable.
The R4 and R6 snapshots both contain the same 19 `OperationOutcome` element ids; no local elements were added, removed, renamed, moved, split, or merged.
All local cardinalities are unchanged, including `issue` at `1..*`, `issue.severity` and `issue.code` at `1..1`, and optional detail/diagnostic/location/expression elements.
No local datatype, choice-type, or reference target changes were found. `issue.details` remains `CodeableConcept`; severity/code remain primitive `code`; location/expression remain `string`.
`OperationOutcome` local elements do not introduce reference-typed fields, so no local reference target set changed.

No local OperationOutcome-specific invariant was added or removed. Constraint expression differences observed on root/domain/extension elements are inherited from base artifacts and intentionally excluded.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value was found in either version.
No local `maxLength`, minValue, maxValue, or regex restriction changed.
No local element changed from non-modifier to modifier or vice versa. R6 explicitly records `isModifier=false` on local elements where R4 relied on the same effective value.
Local summary flags are stable for `issue` and its child elements. Inherited summary flag changes were excluded.
No local slicing definitions or slice rules were present or changed.
Local semantic text is mostly unchanged. R6 adds non-strict guidance about aligning `issue.code` and `issue.severity`; this is captured with the IssueType terminology finding.
No local JSON/XML element names, primitive/value representation, or choice-element serialization pattern changed.

The only local R6-to-R4 representability risks found are required-binding code additions on `issue.severity` and `issue.code`. Exact downstream impact depends on each converter's policy for unknown or unmappable codes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 differential explicitly records false flags on local elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 includes explicit `isModifier=false` and/or `mustSupport=false` entries on local OperationOutcome elements where R4 either had the same effective value or omitted the flag. An explicit false does not add a conformance obligation or change instance validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Schema/code generators that diff raw ElementDefinition JSON should normalize absent booleans and explicit `false` to avoid noisy false positives.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds a W5 mapping for OperationOutcome
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 differential adds a W5 mapping (`infrastructure.exchange`) at the root. Mappings are metadata and do not affect instance validation or wire format.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Mapping-aware documentation or analytics tooling may show a new classification for the resource, but no data transform is required.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `OperationOutcome.language`, `id`, `meta`, and `implicitRules` changes observed in the snapshot are inherited and should be assessed in the base `Resource` report.
Root `dom-*` constraint expression changes, contained-resource wording/conditions, narrative condition references, and `modifierExtension` summary behavior are inherited from `DomainResource`.
Extension invariant placement and generic `ele-1` wording changes appear inherited from the base element/extension definitions rather than local OperationOutcome design.
